justification: Assessment reported INVALID and targeted exactly the ground-truth defect: the converse-direction claim (lines 0074/0078) that pairing the i-th bipartite cover graph on X with the i-th on Y yields 2^{k-1} unions (naive 2^k), when it actually yields k-1 (naive 2(k-1)). Its witness (k=2, K_4: only one index i, so one union graph, not 2; and k=3 giving 3 not 2^{k-1}+1=5 > k) is a different-but-valid instance of the same false identity 2^{k-1} = k-1 that the ground-truth witness (k=4, K_16) certifies. Both also note the same downstream consequence: the claimed count would use more than k graphs for k >= 3, breaking the bound being proved.
